tool: rl/tools/bench.py (isolated executable copies; see docs/rl_throughput_m6.md, section Residual attribution)
note: Attribution experiments only. None of these configurations is implemented as a BattleShip feature by M6; they were run against a copy of build-us/Release in a scratch directory whose BattleShip.cfg.json was edited, with SSB64_RL_NO_RENDER=1 and SSB64_RL_TIMING=1 in the child environment. The repository executable and config were not modified.

temporary_per_thread_profile.method: temporary (reverted, never committed) steady-clock accumulation around every port_coroutine_resume in port_resume_service_threads and around the PortPushFrame segments; averages per unparked frame over 500 frames of the 7.43 s baseline replay through the M1d client
temporary_per_thread_profile.thread_ids: decomp/src/sys/main.c: 3 scheduler, 4 audio, 6 controller (syControllerThreadMain), 5 game, 1 idle

experiment_audio_null_backend.configuration: Window.AudioBackend = null in the copied BattleShip.cfg.json, SSB64_RL_NO_RENDER=1
experiment_audio_null_backend.conclusion: no change: the audio output path is not the residual

experiment_raphnet_native_adapter_disabl.configuration: CVars.gControllers.Raphnet.Enabled = 0 in the copied BattleShip.cfg.json (Window.AudioBackend back to wasapi), SSB64_RL_NO_RENDER=1; a Raphnet N64 USB adapter (vid 0x289b pid 0x0032, firmware 3.4.0) is attached to this machine and libultraship polls it over USB HID at every controller read
experiment_raphnet_native_adapter_disabl.conclusion: the residual pre-read segment is the native adapter poll; without it the no-render step is about 0.5 ms and 1..6 processes scale to about 7400 steps/s

raphnet_bypass_final.note: M6 follow-up, final implementation measured on the final executable (sha256 57d61fe0b2a60265..., git 1868008 + the uncommitted follow-up). The experiment_raphnet_native_adapter_disabled section above is the original isolated-copy experiment and is kept unchanged as historical context.
